tagline: Back up repo docs to Google Drive and link design assets to code repos
metaTitle: GitHub Google Drive Integration: Back Up Docs and Assets
metaDescription: Keep repository docs safe and easy to share outside GitHub. GAIA backs them up to Google Drive and saves release notes on every release. See the setup steps.
intro:
Development teams keep code in GitHub and shared files in Google Drive, but the two rarely reference each other. A design asset in the shared folders has no link to the pull request that implements it. Documentation written in Markdown is not accessible to non-technical stakeholders who live in Google Docs. When a repository is archived or a team offboards, the context that lived only in the repo is not always preserved alongside the project files.

GAIA links the two to create a persistent bridge between code and file storage. Repository documentation can be automatically backed up to matching folders at regular intervals or when significant changes are merged. Design assets, mockups, and specification documents stored in the folders can be automatically linked to relevant pull requests. Non-technical stakeholders get read-only access to documentation through the folders without needing a repository account.

This is especially useful for agencies, consultancies, and product companies that need to deliver documentation to clients (who work in the shared folders), for compliance-driven teams that must keep documentation artifacts outside the repo, and for any team that wants long-term project context stored in Google Drive, with its richer file management capabilities.

useCases.title: Auto-backup repository docs to Google Drive
useCases.description: GAIA watches merged pull requests that change documentation files, exports the updated Markdown files to the matching folder, and converts them to Google Docs format for easy stakeholder access.

useCases.title: Link design assets to new pull requests
useCases.description: When a pull request is opened that implements a feature with matching design assets in the folders, GAIA adds a comment to the pull request with direct links to the relevant files so reviewers can check the implementation against design specifications without leaving the repo.

useCases.title: Organize the folders to match repository structure
useCases.description: GAIA can mirror your repository structure in a folder, creating subfolders for documentation, design, and meeting notes that align with the repository layout so project context is organized consistently across both platforms.

useCases.title: Share release notes to Google Drive on each release
useCases.description: When a new release is published, GAIA exports the release notes to a Google Doc in the project's folder, making the changelog accessible to non-technical stakeholders, clients, and the broader organization without requiring repository access.

useCases.title: Notify team when design assets are updated
useCases.description: When a designer updates a file linked to an open pull request, GAIA posts a comment on that pull request alerting the developer and reviewer that the design spec has changed, reducing the risk of shipping an implementation based on outdated designs.

howItWorks.step: Connect GitHub and Google Drive to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authenticate your repositories and your Google Drive account through GAIA's integration settings. Specify which repositories should be monitored and which folder or Shared Drive should serve as the documentation destination.

Tell GAIA which file types to sync, how often to run backups, how to name and organize files, and which folders contain assets that should be linked back to the repository. You can set per-repository or organization-wide rules.

howItWorks.step: GAIA keeps both sides in sync automatically
howItWorks.description: GAIA watches the repositories for documentation changes and the folders for asset updates, running sync and notification workflows automatically. Your team's file storage always reflects the current state of the codebase and vice versa.

faqs.question: Can GAIA export GitHub Wiki pages as well as repository files?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA can export Wiki pages to the destination folder in addition to repository Markdown files. Wiki exports are converted to Google Docs format so they are fully editable and accessible to non-technical collaborators who need to contribute to documentation.

faqs.question: How does GAIA match files to pull requests?
faqs.answer: GAIA uses folder structure conventions, file naming patterns, and labels or branch names in the repo to identify matching assets. You can also include a folder link in a pull request description or configure explicit mappings between repository paths and folders.

faqs.question: Does GAIA support Google Shared Drives for team-wide storage?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA works with both personal storage and Google Shared Drives (formerly Team Drives), making it suitable for organizations that manage all project files in a centralized Shared Drive accessible to the whole team.
